title: In Vivo Experiments of Anti-Cancer Treatments in Mice
author: Randall J Kimple

steps.title: Define experimental design parameters
steps.instruction: Decide species/strain (e.g., mouse – BALB/c Nude, SCID), anatomical site (e.g., bilateral flank), number of study groups (e.g., 4 groups: Control, Drug, Radiation, Drug + Radiation), animals per group (e.g., 12 athymic mice per group), early‑sacrifice time points (e.g., 8 h, 24 h, 48 h) and samples per early sacrifice (e.g., 4 tumors per group), total experiment duration (e.g., 7, 14 or 21 days), treatment frequency (e.g., 2 × day, 5 days / week), route of administration (e.g., Cetuximab intraperitoneal, other drugs oral gavage), drug/radiation dose and volume, radiation timing (≥1 h after drug), and primary metrics (e.g., tumor size measured with calipers).

steps.title: Obtain ethical approvals and training
steps.instruction: Secure an approved Institutional Review Board (IRB) / Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) protocol and ensure all personnel are trained in animal handling, anesthesia, irradiation, and euthanasia procedures.

steps.title: Order animals and extra supplies
steps.instruction: Order the required number of animals plus 3–4 extras (e.g., 12 × 4 = 48 mice + extra), and confirm availability of animal facilities, irradiator, anesthesia equipment, and other needed hardware.

steps.title: Secure starting material and consumables
steps.instruction: Ensure sufficient starting material (e.g., for 40 mice with bilateral flank injections → 80 injections, need ~2–3 g tumor tissue for a PDX experiment) and consumables such as Matrigel and culture media.

steps.title: Prepare drug stock and vehicle
steps.instruction: Calculate total drug amount needed for the entire study, order the drug, and confirm the vehicle solution for making the working stock that will be used for the control arm.

steps.title: Implant or inject tumor material
steps.instruction: Inject/implant the PDX or cell line into the predetermined anatomical site (e.g., bilateral flank) of each mouse according to the planned volume and matrix (e.g., Matrigel).

steps.title: Set up documentation and randomization plan
steps.instruction: Create a master document containing: a) treatment schedule, b) table of treatment, route, dose, volume, and dose calculations, c) randomization scheme, d) tumor‑measurement fields, e) tumor volume calculations, f) animal weights, g) animal identifiers (e.g., ear tag numbers). Ensure the document allows another experimenter to reproduce the study.

steps.title: Monitor pre‑treatment tumor growth
steps.instruction: Monitor each mouse at least twice a week until tumors reach the predefined initiation size (average 150–200 mm³ per mouse). Record tumor dimensions with calipers and animal weights.

steps.title: Randomize mice into treatment groups
steps.instruction: When the initiation point is reached, average the two flank tumor volumes per mouse, then assign mice to groups to achieve similar average tumor size per group. Separate mice into group‑specific cages, labeling cages and animals (e.g., ear tag or ear punch); allow ~2 hours for this process.

steps.title: Administer treatments according to schedule
steps.instruction: Begin treatment per the pre‑designed schedule (e.g., drug 2 × day, 5 days / week; radiation given at least 1 h after drug). Use the specified routes (e.g., Cetuximab intraperitoneal, other drugs oral gavage).

steps.title: Perform early sacrifices if planned
steps.instruction: If early sacrifice was defined (e.g., after first 48 h of treatment), euthanize the designated mice, collect the predetermined number of tumors (e.g., 4 per group), and process for paraffin embedding and fast‑frozen DNA extraction.

steps.title: Record growth metrics twice weekly
steps.instruction: Measure tumor size with calipers and weigh animals at least twice a week (e.g., Monday and Thursday), entering data into the documentation sheet.

steps.title: Conclude treatment and decide final sacrifice timing
steps.instruction: After the full treatment period (7, 14 or 21 days), determine whether to euthanize immediately for final sample collection or to continue monitoring before sacrifice.

steps.title: Euthanize animals per approved protocol
steps.instruction: Euthanize mice using the institution‑approved method (e.g., CO₂ followed by cervical dislocation).

steps.title: Collect and label tissue samples
steps.instruction: Harvest all samples specified in the experimental design, label each sample clearly, and record its storage location in the documentation sheet.
